iFixit 的 teardown of the new AirPods 5 has revealed a small but important repairability improvement. Check out the video below.

A record-breaking repairability score: 2 out of 10

Since Apple launched the first AirPods in 2016, iFixit has consistently given them a repairability score of 0 out of 10. From batteries that are held in place with strong adhesive and soldered connections, to housings that can barely be opened and reassembled without causing damage, AirPods have always been extremely difficult to repair.

However, with the new AirPods 5, iFixit says Apple has taken a small step in the right direction, provided the repair work is carried out by a skilled professional or a particularly adventurous DIY enthusiast.

In their latest teardown video, iFixit demonstrated that the battery inside each earbud can be removed and replaced without destroying the AirPods, earning AirPods their first-ever non-zero repairability score.

Granted, the new AirPods 5 only scored 2 out of 10, but that's still two points higher than every previous model combined.

iFixit points out that the left and right batteries cannot be swapped, as they use opposite polarity and have slightly different contact point positions.

That said, that's essentially the extent of the AirPods 5's repairability. As iFixit showed in the video, any further disassembly of the earbuds will still destroy them, and the same goes for the charging case.

iFixit's teardown also includes their always-fascinating CT scan images, which provide a detailed look at how Apple crams the battery, MEMS microphone, H2 chip, and other tiny components densely into each earbud.
